gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Bold wire-bent signage comes to mind with Tilt Neon, its stroke constant and its c terminal splayed. And Noto Sans Khojki carries paragraph after paragraph smoothly, its wide exits and big-eyed e letting light through.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Bold tube-like lines in Tilt Neon outline every counter in one steady thickness. Noto Sans Khudawadi leaves its rounds unsealed and its capitals close to lowercase height, which is the friendliest quality of the pair.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-kr: Bold outlines in a single width give Tilt Neon its tubing look, ascenders kept short. Noto Sans KR keeps its curves generously open and its ascenders stubby, a clean counterweight to all that outline.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-lao: Noto Sans Lao pushes its x-height well above the usual, with its mouths left open. But Tilt Neon draws strokes that never thicken or thin, and that shared tallness ties the two together.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-lao-looped: Noto Sans Lao Looped reads in solid word blocks rather than ragged skylines, its bowls left unfinished on one side. But shrink Tilt Neon and its single-width stroke loses the bold, wire-bent presence that makes it worth using.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Bold tubular letters in Tilt Neon carry no stroke contrast to slow the eye. Noto Sans Lepcha brings approachable, wide-opening curves and a lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Tilt Neon draws every stroke at a single thickness, with a splayed c terminal and short ascenders. And Noto Sans Limbu counters with tall-bodied small letters and gaping curves, which is what makes the pair feel approachable.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Bold, rounded strokes like cut lengths of cord give Tilt Neon its signage presence. But Tilt Neon grabs attention while Noto Sans Lisu handles the text with tiny ascender gaps.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-lydian: A splayed c terminal and tube-like, constant-width strokes make Tilt Neon instantly recognizable. But Tilt Neon earns its keep big and short, while Noto Sans Lydian keeps capitals barely taller than lowercase.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Tube-like strokes of constant width, ending in a splayed c, make Tilt Neon read like bent wire. Noto Sans Mahajani stands its lowercase tall against the capitals, so a small Tilt Neon would lose ground to it.
